messages.content: is maybe she is home the same idea as she may be home?
yes. both can leave it open whether she is home.
can i write she maybe home?
use she may be home, with may and be as two words. or use maybe she is home.
why is is in only the maybe example?
maybe is one word used with the full sentence she is home. may be works as part of the sentence after she.
use simple words for that difference.
write maybe she is home, or she may be home. do not put maybe in place of is by itself.
what if i know she is home?
then say she is home. maybe and may be would make it sound like you are not sure.
make that explanation shorter.
leave maybe out when you know.
only give the two open answers again.
maybe she is home. she may be home.
write a longer story about someone asking for the last book and meaning the one read before, while another person thinks it is the book at the end of a line.

a child put four books in a line on the table. her father asked to see the last book. she gave him the one at the far end of the line. he looked at it and said it was not the story he wanted to ask about. he wanted the book she read before the one she was reading now. she had heard last as a place in the line, while he had used it for the reading before now. they found the right book by talking about the story rather than saying last again. after that, he asked for the book about the family at the park, and she knew which one to bring. the line of books had stayed the same. the question was how the word last was being used.
why did she bring the book from the end of the line?
she thought last was about its place in the line.
what did her father want?
the book she read before the one she was reading now.
make that answer more simple.
he wanted the book she read before this one.
write a more clear request from him.
could you bring the book you read before this one, the story about the family at the park?
finish with them looking at the same page.
she opened the book to a picture she remembered, and he asked about the people in it.
six people said they would come. all but two came. how many came?
four people came.
can you know which two did not come?
no. the number does not tell us which people they were.
make that explanation shorter.
no. how many is not who.
now i say one was my sister and the other was my aunt.
then your sister and your aunt were the two who did not come.
can you know why?
no. you gave who, but not their reasons.
only give the number who came again.
four.
what does the next page mean?
it usually is the page after the one you are on now, or after the page being talked about.
make that explanation shorter.
it is the page after the one you mean now.
what if i am on page two?
if the page order is one, two, three, then the next page after two is three.
only give the answer about page two.
the next page after two is three.
can next change when i move to another page?
yes. it is about the page after your new place. the word does not always name one fixed page.
use words without fixed.
next can be a different page when you begin from a different place.
only give the answer for page two again.
the next page is page three.
write a longer story about a child asking for a short answer first, then choosing to hear more once the first idea is clear.

a child asked her aunt why the book on the table had a different picture from the one at home. her aunt began a long explanation about how books could be made and changed over time. the child stopped her in a kind way and asked whether the story inside could still be the same. her aunt said yes. that short answer gave the child the part she needed first. then she wanted to know why the pictures might be different, so they looked at both books together. she had not asked for less because she never wanted to learn more. she needed a clear start before the other details would be useful. the aunt waited for the next question rather than giving every detail at once.
what did the child need to know first?
whether the story inside could still be the same.
was the short answer enough for every question she might have?
no. it answered the first part. she asked for more when ready.
make the important idea in that story more simple.
the longer explanation was useful after the first part was clear.
make that answer shorter.
a clear start helped her learn more.
finish with them choosing one picture to talk about.
she showed her aunt the picture at the start and asked why the person looked that way. her aunt looked at the page with her.
i finished reading the book, but i do not remember every detail. help me say both.
i finished reading the book, but i do not remember every detail.
can i still say i enjoyed it?
yes, if you did enjoy it. you can enjoy a book without keeping every detail in your mind.
make that answer shorter.
you do not need every detail to enjoy it.
put that into one sentence in my voice.
i enjoyed reading the book, even though i do not remember every detail.
does that say i understood nothing in it?
no. it only says you do not remember every detail. that is different from understanding nothing.
make that explanation shorter.
not keeping every detail is different from understanding nothing.
only give my sentence again.
i enjoyed reading the book, even though i do not remember every detail.
write a longer story about two people leaving messages about the same object. the messages should be about different parts of the day, so both can work.

a brother left a note saying he needed the table for reading in the morning. his sister later left a note saying she needed it for drawing after lunch. when their father saw both pages, he thought they were asking for the table at the same time. he began looking for another place for one of them. then he read the time words. one request was for the morning, and the other was for after lunch. both could use the same table if each put their things away at the end. he did not need to choose one request over the other. they only needed a clear change between the two parts of the day. that evening, the table was free for the family meal too.
why did the father first look for another place?
he thought the two people needed the table at the same time.
what made both plans possible?
they were for different parts of the day.
give that answer as a sentence about the two pages.
the two pages did not ask for the table at once. each gave a different time.
what did each person need to do after using it?
put their things away so the next person could use the table.
finish with the morning book ready on the shelf.
the brother put his book away before lunch. his sister found the space clear when she brought her paper.
can i am still reading and i have not finished yet both be true?
yes. they can both say the reading is not done.
what does still add?
it says you were reading before and are reading now too.
make that answer shorter.
the reading is still happening now.
what does not finished yet say?
it says finishing has not happened up to now, while often leaving later open.
can i say not finished yet if i stopped for a break?
yes. you may not be reading at this moment, but you have not finished the book.
make that answer shorter.
yes. a break does not finish the book.
what would i say to make that clear?
i have not finished yet. i am taking a break.
only give the two first sentences again.
i am still reading. i have not finished yet.
my friend changed the meeting place. i need the new place, not an idea about why they changed it.
where should we meet now?
can i add that i saw the change?
i saw that the place changed. where should we meet now?
why not ask if they feel sad?
because the place change alone does not tell you that feeling. your task is to find the new place.
only give the message about the place again.
i saw that the place changed. where should we meet now?
what if i also need to know whether the time changed?
ask that too: did the time change as well, or only the place?
put both questions in one message.
where should we meet now? did the time change too, or only the place?
only give the time question.
did the time change too, or only the place?
write a longer story about a child seeing three on a page and not knowing whether it is pages, minutes, or people. show why the word after the number helps.

a child found a small note near a book with only three written on it. he thought it was about reading three pages, because that was what he had been doing. his sister thought it might be a time to meet, and their mother asked whether it was the number of people coming. they did not have enough context to choose. when their father returned, he explained that he had wanted to say three minutes until he would be ready to help. by then, the time itself was no longer useful, but the conversation was. next time, he wrote the number with minutes and gave a starting time too. a number could be correct and still leave out the part needed to use it.
why could they not use three by itself?
they did not know whether it was about pages, time, or people.
make that explanation shorter.
they needed more than the number.
what did the father mean?
he was talking about three minutes until he would be ready.
make the difference between the place and meaning of the note clear.
the note was near the book, but it was about a waiting time, not reading pages.
finish with the next message clear.
he wrote that he needed three minutes from now. the child knew there was time to finish one short sentence before asking for help.
my teacher asked what i wanted to say, and that helped me fix my sentence more than a new sentence would have.
the question gave you room to find your own meaning before changing the words.
can you help me explain that without saying answers are never useful?
you could say: that question helped me understand my own idea. sometimes an answer helps too, but this time i needed to think first.
can i make it shorter?
your question helped me find what i wanted to say.
what if i still needed a word after that?
then asking for that word could be the next useful step. finding your idea and finding the words can be different parts of the task.
only give the thank you for the question.
thank you. your question helped me find what i wanted to say.
why not say i did it without help?
because the question was part of the help you said you used.
say hello, but do not say how my day has been.
hello. it is nice to hear from you.
now just hello.
hello.
now a goodbye in two words.
take care.
only goodbye instead.
goodbye.
